author: ViceTechnicolour
body:
I don't understand the point of blocking commands for convenience purposes. If I can do the exact same but with an extra step or two, I don't see why players should be limited for it and backed only by it being "for staff".

/history is already accessible on the site, why can't we check in-game? There's moments where a player may want to record someone suspicious of breaking the rules to help out, but you need to use the website (which I don't see why is necessary)

replies.body:
/go is already implemented for players (I can use it at least)
/history is a no. Why care how many offences a player has, if you see him rule breaking just gain evidence and report. It shouldn't matter if he has a good history or not to gain evidence. And tbh don't start following people just to see if they are breaking the rules again if they had a bad history. That could be considered harassment. Your not a mod, your a player. A player's job is to do /report and to gain evidence of a player breaking the rules said player starts breaking that said rule. If he has not started you shouldn't start spectating him trying to gain evidence

replies.author: ViceTechnicolour
replies.body:
I didn't mean it in that sense/context (or lack thereof). I meant that if a player breaks the rules toward you, I'd personally want to know their infractions. If I'm in-game being griefed and killed, I can't take a look on the site and wait for it to load, or I'll be dead. It's better to run a fast command for it.

I would also take action in recording if they had previous punishments for it, for sure. If they had none, I'd probably just leave it to /report anyway because I wouldn't have time to also take out my recorder for it too. As said, convenience is important.

replies.author: ViceTechnicolour
replies.body:
I'm confused.

If a player is breaking the rules, they will be punished.
Less accessibility to look their infractions up will give more time for them to grief.
If a player can look it up on the site, you should be able to in-game anyway.
Making it harder to find it would be on the reporter's end, not the griefer.
Punish players who harass them, but no problem in recording a player who breaks the rules even if you stalked them for a few minutes.
